sources.entry: Compass - Landing page for services, dashboards, and documents, with automatic discovery from sources such as Docker, Kubernetes, and Tailscale. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Compass is a self-hosted landing page that automatically discovers and displays services, dashboards, and documents from sources such as Docker, Kubernetes, and Tailscale.
summary.what_it_does: Compass reads a YAML config that lists one or more service sources and renders what those sources expose as a server-driven web UI. The README names Docker, Kubernetes, Tailscale, Headscale, static config, and JSON API sources. It shows per-source health and refresh status, along with service metadata, panels, tags, and debug views. Users can search, filter, and jump into discovered services without writing hand-maintained cards. The UI is server-rendered HTML using HTMX, Alpine.js, Tailwind, and daisyUI. The README gives Docker and Helm (OCI chart) quick-start examples for running it.
use_cases: browse tailscale or headscale machines and services
central page for internal dashboards and documents
how_to_run: Write a compass.yaml with an organization name and a docker source (type: docker, name: local)

docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --group-add $(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3) -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro -v $PWD/compass.yaml:/etc/compass/compass.yaml:ro adinhodovic/compass:latest -c /etc/compass/compass.yaml
For Kubernetes, write compass.yaml with a kubernetes source (type: kubernetes) and namespaces: []
helm install compass oci://ghcr.io/adinhodovic/charts/compass -n compass --create-namespace --set-file config=compass.yaml
notable: Automatic discovery from Docker, Kubernetes, Tailscale, and Headscale sources
Source health and refresh status shown in the UI
Helm chart installs with in-cluster RBAC for Kubernetes discovery
Server-rendered HTML UI with HTMX and Alpine.js rather than a heavy SPA
caveats: Docker source needs access to the Docker socket; the README suggests adding the host docker GID or using a socket proxy such as tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy
Kubernetes setup relies on Helm-granted in-cluster RBAC for discovery
README points to separate Getting started and Docs pages for fuller configuration; the README itself gives only minimal examples
